international.canonicalTopic: Anak Krakatau eruption and flight disruption
international.headline: Anak Krakatau eruption disrupts flights in Jakarta
facts: Anak Krakatau erupted on 2026-09-06 in Indonesia’s Sunda Strait; volcanic ash disrupted flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno–Hatta and Halim Perdanakusuma international airports and several regional airports.
Anak Krakatau is an active volcanic island between Java and Sumatra, formed in the caldera region created by the 1883 Krakatau eruption; its name means “Child of Krakatau.”
The Sunda Strait separates Java and Sumatra and connects the Java Sea with the Indian Ocean.
Indonesia is in the Pacific Ring of Fire, where plate interactions, particularly at subduction zones, contribute to frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
international.summary: The eruption of Anak Krakatau sent ash that disrupted flights in Jakarta and at regional airports, highlighting the aviation and disaster risks of volcanic activity.
international.staticLink: Pacific Ring of Fire; Sunda Strait; volcanic hazards and ash-related aviation disruption.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Anak Krakatau lies in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra; the 1883 Krakatau eruption created the caldera from which it emerged.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how volcanic ash hazards require coordination between disaster-management agencies, aviation authorities and public services.

national.canonicalTopic: India–China Corps Commander-level meeting at Wacha–Damai
national.headline: India and China hold Corps Commander-level talks at Arunachal Pradesh border point
facts: India and China held a Corps Commander-level military meeting on September 6, 2026, at the Indian side of the Wacha–Damai Border Personnel Meeting point in the Kibithu sector of Anjaw district, Arunachal Pradesh.

The sides discussed border management, de-escalation, military communication, management of border incidents and prevention of local tensions along the eastern sector of the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
The meeting was described in the notes as the first Corps Commander-level meeting held at Wacha–Damai, which has been operational since 2014.
The notes report that earlier talks at this level were mainly held at Chushul–Moldo in eastern Ladakh.
The meeting followed reports of increased military deployment and local tensions in the Taksing area of Upper Subansiri district.
National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi had earlier met in Beijing on August 25, 2026, to discuss border management and peace along the LAC.
The notes describe the LAC as a de facto line, not a mutually agreed formal international boundary; they place Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim in the eastern sector.
national.summary: Commanders met at the Wacha–Damai BPM point in Arunachal Pradesh to discuss border management and mechanisms for preventing local tensions.
national.staticLink: The India–China border is described in western, middle and eastern sectors; the eastern sector includes Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Wacha–Damai is in the Kibithu sector of Anjaw district; the meeting took place on the Indian side of the BPM point.
national.mainsAngle: Examine the role of military communication mechanisms and local border meetings in preventing escalation along the LAC.
national.apLink: The meeting was held at Kibithu in Anjaw district, Arunachal Pradesh.

national.canonicalTopic: 16th National Meeting of State Biodiversity Boards
national.headline: National meeting of biodiversity boards held in Chandigarh
facts: The 16th National Meeting of State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils was held in Chandigarh on September 6–7, 2026, organised by the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA).
Discussions focused on biodiversity conservation, sustainable use of biological resources, local implementation and coordination among national, State, Union Territory and local institutions.

India’s three-tier biodiversity governance system comprises the NBA at the national level, State Biodiversity Boards or UT Biodiversity Councils at the State or UT level, and Biodiversity Management Committees at the local level.

Biodiversity Management Committees help document and conserve local biological resources and associated traditional knowledge; People’s Biodiversity Registers record local biodiversity and related knowledge.
The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 was enacted to implement India’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
The NBA was established in 2003 and is headquartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu.
The CBD was signed at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and entered into force in 1993; its objectives include conservation, sustainable use and fair and equitable sharing of benefits.
The Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, adopted at CBD COP15 in 2022, includes a target to conserve at least 30% of terrestrial, inland water, coastal and marine areas by 2030.
national.summary: The meeting addressed biodiversity governance and coordination across the national, State, UT and local tiers, including implementation of the Biological Diversity Act.
national.staticLink: India’s biodiversity governance operates through the NBA, State and UT bodies, and local Biodiversity Management Committees under the framework of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The NBA is headquartered in Chennai; the CBD’s three objectives are conservation, sustainable use and fair and equitable benefit-sharing.
national.mainsAngle: Assess the contribution of local biodiversity documentation and benefit-sharing institutions to decentralised conservation.

national.notes:
# 1. Meeting details
- **Event:** **16th National Meeting of State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils**; completed
- **When:** **6–7 September 2026**
- **Where:** **Chandigarh**
- **Organiser:** **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)**
- **Discussions:** Biodiversity conservation; sustainable use of biological resources; local implementation; coordination among national, State, Union Territory and local institutions

# 2. Biodiversity governance
- **Three-tier system:**
| Level | Institution | Role / scope stated |
|---|---|---|
| National | **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)** | National-level body |
| State / UT | **State Biodiversity Boards** or **UT Biodiversity Councils** | State- or UT-level bodies |
| Local | **Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)** | Help document and conserve local biological resources and associated traditional knowledge |
- **People’s Biodiversity Registers (PBRs):** Record local biodiversity and related knowledge
- **NBA established:** **2003**
- **Headquarters:** **Chennai, Tamil Nadu**
- **Andhra Pradesh link:** No direct AP-specific link established

# 3. Legal and global framework
- **Act:** **Biological Diversity Act, 2002**; enacted to implement India’s obligations under the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**
- **CBD:** Signed at the **1992 Rio Earth Summit**; entered into force in **1993**
- **CBD objectives:** Conservation of biological diversity; sustainable use of its components; fair and equitable sharing of benefits
- **Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework:** Adopted at **CBD COP15** in **2022**
- **2030 target:** Conserve at least **30%** of terrestrial, inland water, coastal and marine areas by **2030**
- ⚠ **Trap:** **BMCs** are the local-level bodies; **PBRs** are records of local biodiversity and related knowledge, not a separate tier of biodiversity governance.
> Exam angle: Test the **NBA–State/UT bodies–BMC** governance tiers, the **CBD’s three objectives**, and the framework’s **30% by 2030** target.
